projects.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.
